payload.rebuttal: fixed: The sub-cap witness passed emit=lambda line: None, so it never checked what write_follow_ups logged; a mutant dropping the reason from _pool's `pooled {task_key} {file}: {reason}` line survived since the Pooled object's own reason field was untouched. I changed the test to capture emitted lines (emit=emitted.append) and added an assertion that each of the four Pooled entries' reason, including the three owned ones, appears verbatim on its own `pooled ...: reason` line. I reproduced the named mutant against a scratch copy of saffron/follow_up.py and confirmed the new assertion fails on it before restoring the real file and committing.
